line_outage_by_pair: put the transmission corridor between buses (\d+) and (\d+) out of service
corridor between buses (\d+) and (\d+) out of service
knock the (\d+)-(\d+) corridor out of service
target_pq_scale_factor: ([0-9]*\.?[0-9]+)% more on both active and reactive
target_pv_bus: generator-side voltage-control record associated with bus (\d+)

prompt_guidance: Treat `corridor between buses A and B`, `trip the branch`, and `out of service` phrasing as line-outage requests that should map to `ssa.Line.set_status(...)` after resolving the real line idx.
For contingency studies, update line status through `ssa.Line.set_status(...)`. Do not invent helpers such as `ssa.PFlow.set(..., attr='in_service', ...)`.
Treat `outage set`, `screening set`, or `stressed case` wording as N-1 screening over the listed candidate bus pairs, always restarting from the same modified case.
Interpret phrases like `4% heavier` or `3% higher` on the same demand record as multiplying both `p0` and `q0` by `1.04` or `1.03`.
Treat phrases such as `regulator target`, `voltage-control record`, or `generator-side voltage-control record` as PV `v0` adjustment requests.
ANDES device identifiers such as `PQ_2` or `Line_3` may be strings; preserve them as returned by ANDES instead of forcing integer conversion.
When the user identifies a demand or PV record by bus, resolve the matching device idx from the real ANDES arrays before calling `.set(...)`.
Do not treat the bus number or array position as the device idx for `PQ`, `PV`, or `Line` edits.

root_cause_summary.label: String device idx was cast to int
Bus number or array index was used as device idx
Open-ended percentage demand phrasing was not grounded
Open-ended regulator phrasing was not grounded
Corridor phrasing was not mapped to line outage status edits
Outage-set language was not mapped to N-1 screening
